'''Decipher, Inc.''' (often just '''Decipher''') was the Norfolk, Virginia&ndash;area game company that published the printed ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) from December 1995 through 2001.<ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia</ref>

This wiki page is a '''fan encyclopedia hub''' for Decipher-as-SWCCG-publisher. It is not the company and does not republish Decipher corporate materials in full. Sister encyclopedias with broader company coverage include the [https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher LOTR-TCG Players Council Decipher page] and Wikipedia.

[[File:Decipher logo 1999.jpg|thumb|right|220px|1999 corporate lockup with brushstroke mark and tagline ''The Art of Great Games'' (preserved on the LOTR-TCG wiki).]]

== Founder / leadership ==

[[Warren Holland]] founded Decipher in '''1983''' and appears on Decipher's own About pages (c. 2000) as '''Chairman &amp; CEO''' / Founder and CEO, with headquarters in downtown Norfolk, Virginia.<ref name="ia-about">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/index.html About Decipher], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000)</ref><ref name="ia-findus">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/findus/ Find Us], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000)</ref><ref name="wp-decipher" /> See the Holland page for Vision statement, press path, license-loss / Players' Committee statements, and interview links.

== Early years (puzzles and party games) ==

Decipher began in 1983 with contest jigsaw puzzles marketed under the Decipher name, then built a long-running party-game line around ''How to Host a Murder'', and later marketed ''Pente'' after acquiring that license from Parker Brothers.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="ia-vision">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/vision/ Vision], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000) — company statement signed Warren Holland, Chairman and CEO, citing inception in 1983</ref> The company's own slogan of the CCG era was '''Decipher: The Art of Great Games'''.<ref name="wook-decipher">[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Decipher Decipher], Wookieepedia</ref><ref name="lotr-decipher">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki</ref>

== CCG era (overview) ==

After ''Magic: The Gathering'' popularized collectible card games, designers [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] pitched a media-licensed CCG approach; Decipher's first major CCG was ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' (1994), followed by SWCCG (1995) and later titles including ''Austin Powers'', ''Young Jedi'', ''Jedi Knights'', ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG, several youth-market licenses (''.hack'', ''Beyblade'', ''Mega Man''), the original-IP ''WARS'' TCG, and finally ''Fight Klub''.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="lotr-decipher" /> At peak, Star Wars CCG sales were among the top non-''Magic'' CCGs.<ref name="lotr-decipher" /><ref name="wp-decipher" />

This hub keeps '''SWCCG detail local''' (see sections below and the expansion tiles on the [[Main Page]]). Sister wikis carry deeper LOTR / Star Trek product narratives.

== SWCCG ==

Decipher released SWCCG after acquiring a Lucasfilm license, following earlier success with ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG.<ref name="wp-decipher" /> Designers commonly credited for SWCCG are summarized on [[Creators of SWCCG]] ([[Tom Braunlich]], [[Rollie Tesh]], [[Jerry Darcy]], [[Warren Holland]]).<ref name="wp-swccg" />

Printed Decipher sets on this wiki begin with [[Premiere Limited]] (December 1995) and continue through the Decipher expansion list on the [[Main Page]].

== After the license ==

When Decipher lost the ''Star Wars'' license (contract non-renewal; Wizards of the Coast / Hasbro relationship with Lucasfilm is the usual sister-wiki framing), company leadership publicly supported a Players' Committee / advocate structure so organized play and later virtual cards could continue.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="hist">[[History of the Players Committee]]</ref><ref name="lotr-decipher" /> For the license fight, July 2000 Lucasfilm presentation excerpts, December 2001 end, and handoff context see [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]]. Stewardship after 2001 is community/Players Committee history, not Decipher product.

== Decline (high level) ==

Sister encyclopedias describe a multi-year contraction after license losses and underperforming launches: FanHQ / fan-club magazine efforts faded as social media grew; ''WARS'' and several youth CCGs struggled; RPG lines were cut; staff reductions compounded late-set delays on remaining licensed games; physical product effectively ended after ''Fight Klub'' (c. 2008), while decipher.com continued intermittent "coming back" messaging for years afterward.<ref name="lotr-decipher" /><ref name="wp-decipher" /> Deep SW license chronology stays on [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]]; deep LOTR endgame narrative stays on the LOTR-TCG wiki.

=== Embezzlement (cited) ===

Press and sister-wiki summaries report that former Decipher finance executive '''Rick Eddleman''' (Holland's brother-in-law) was prosecuted for embezzling company funds; a civil judgment and a 2009 criminal sentence (about six years) are documented in contemporary Virginia press. Wikipedia summarizes a guilty plea involving more than US$1.5&nbsp;million and a civil settlement figure near US$8.9&nbsp;million; the LOTR-TCG wiki recounts Holland-hosted document dumps (now archived) estimating losses on the order of US$9&nbsp;million over the 1990s–2001 tenure.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="lotr-decipher" /><ref name="pilot-plea">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090316043101/http://hamptonroads.com/node/501025 Norfolk man pleads guilty to embezzling more than $1.5m], ''The Virginian-Pilot'' (Internet Archive)</ref><ref name="pilot-sentence">[https://web.archive.org/web/20121002195010/http://hamptonroads.com/2009/07/game-company-embezzler-gets-6-years-must-repay-910000 Game company embezzlement was betrayal to family], ''The Virginian-Pilot'' (Internet Archive)</ref><ref name="embezzle-site">[https://web.archive.org/web/20091005031807/http://www.embezzlementfromdecipher.com/ EmbezzlementFromDecipher.com], archived overview hosted by Holland (Internet Archive)</ref> Treat dollar totals and timelines as '''press / sister-wiki reported''' unless a primary court PDF is attached later; do not invent dates beyond the cited captures.
